$comment: English texts of data/events.json (src/engine/overlay.js): every event, with every step, case and outcome, their shared texts and the events' foes. The `classes` and `xpFoes` of an option are ids, not texts.

wounded-woman.title: Wounded Woman
wounded-woman.text: A wounded woman lies by the path. She is pale, barely breathing, and whispers: “Help me…”

dies.name: Questions: dies in despair
dies.text: The woman tries to answer, but your suspicious questions do not help: they take away all her hope of being saved. She dies in despair before your eyes. There is nothing more you can do for her.

wisp.name: Questions: turns into a Strayling
wisp.text: The woman falls silent, offended. Her eyes turn white, her skin begins to glow with a cold light, and her body rises above the path. The wounded woman turns into a Strayling!

outcome.text: You walk away without turning your back on her. No one follows you.

help.text: You lean over her, and three bandits leap out of the bushes. The woman jumps up and runs. It was an ambush!

ask.text: The woman stumbles over her answers, and a twig snaps in the bushes. You sense the ambush before the bandits leap out of hiding.
ask.start: The bandits leap out of hiding, but the ambush no longer takes you by surprise: {enemies}.

help.text: You dress her wound and help her up. The woman thanks you with tears in her eyes and presses a purse of gold into your hand (+{gold}).
You dress her wound and help her up. To thank you, the woman gives you something she found in the forest: {item}.

fern-flower.title: Fern Flower
fern-flower.text: Among the ferns beneath a mossy boulder, a red light glows. It is the fern flower they tell of in every village: whoever picks it will never be forsaken by luck. Something stirred between the boulders.

outcome.text: Not all luck is worth its price. You walk away, and the red light fades behind your back.

pick.text: As you reach for the flower, Misfortune steps out from behind a boulder: gaunt, one-eyed, its hand stretched out for the luck of others.
pick.start: {enemies} stands between you and the flower.

watch.text: Misfortune steps out from behind a boulder. It looks the flower over with its one eye, sniffs and vanishes among the stones. You pick the flower, and in your hand it turns into gold coins (+{gold}).

item.name: Picking: an item
item.text: You pick the flower. It blooms in your hand and crumbles into red dust. Something is left in your palm: {item}.

blossom.name: Picking: a Fern Flower
blossom.text: You pick the flower. It does not fade or crumble into dust: it glows in your hand with a warm red light. You tuck it carefully into your bag (+1 Fern Flower).

watch.text: You wait in hiding, but nothing happens. Towards morning the flower fades and vanishes, as if it had never been there.

fern-flower-calm.name: Fern Flower without Misfortune
fern-flower-calm.title: Fern Flower
fern-flower-calm.text: Among the ferns, a red light glows. It is the fern flower they tell of in every village: whoever picks it will never be forsaken by luck.

item.name: Picking: an item
item.text: You pick the flower. It blooms in your hand and crumbles into red dust. Something is left in your palm: {item}.

blossom.name: Picking: a Fern Flower
blossom.text: You pick the flower. It does not fade or crumble into dust: it glows in your hand with a warm red light. You tuck it carefully into your bag (+1 Fern Flower).

outcome.text: You wait in hiding, but nothing happens. Towards morning the flower fades and vanishes, as if it had never been there.
Not all luck is worth its price. You walk away, and the red light fades behind your back.

blue-mushroom.title: Blue Mushroom
blue-mushroom.text: A mushroom you do not know grows by the path. Its cap glows blue, and tiny shimmering spores float in the air around it. It smells sweet and strange.

faint.name: Eating: fainting
faint.text: You bite off a piece of the cap. The world starts to spin, and blue light floods your eyes. You wake up on the moss when the sun is already low.
faint.lossText: Your purse is noticeably lighter (−{gold} gold).

speed.name: Eating: lightness
speed.text: You bite off a piece of the cap. Your legs itch to run, and every move comes easily (speed in fights +25% for 2 fights).

armor.name: Eating: tough skin
armor.text: You bite off a piece of the cap. Your skin prickles and hardens like the bark of an old oak (armour +15% for 2 fights).

damage.name: Eating: strength
damage.text: You bite off a piece of the cap. Warmth spreads through your arms, and your hands tighten on your weapon of their own accord (damage +10% for 2 fights).

focus.name: Eating: clear mind
focus.text: You bite off a piece of the cap. Your thoughts become clear and sharp as frost at dawn (Intellect and Wisdom +10% for 2 fights).

point.name: Eating: free stat point
point.text: You bite off a piece of the cap. For a moment you see the forest as the System sees it: lines, numbers and the paths between them. When the vision fades, something stays with you (+1 free stat point).

outcome.text: Not everything that glows is fit to eat. You give the mushroom a wide berth and return to the path.

wandering-beggar.title: Wandering Beggar
wandering-beggar.text: An old beggar with a hurdy-gurdy at his side stands by the road. He has holey boots and a grey beard, and holds out an empty cup. He raises his faded eyes: “Spare an old man a penny?”

outcome.text: You pass the beggar without a word. For a while you can still hear the quiet tune of his hurdy-gurdy behind you.

coins.text: You drop a few coins into the cup (−{cost} gold). The beggar traces a sign over you and mumbles a blessing. Your step grows surer and your skin tougher (armour +10% for 2 fights).

song.text: The beggar tunes his hurdy-gurdy and sings an old song about wanderers who never came home. One verse sounds like a warning: “{area}. The {creature} was seen there.”
song.noRumorText: The beggar tunes his hurdy-gurdy and sings an old song about days long gone. It is beautiful, but nothing comes of it.

chase.text: The beggar gathers his things and walks off towards the forest without a word.

coins.text: You drop a few coins into the cup (−{cost} gold). The beggar smiles, and for a moment a green fire lights up in his eyes: “A generous soul. Veles will remember this.” Before you can answer, the road is empty (+1 free stat point).

song.text: The beggar plays a song so beautiful that the whole forest falls silent and the birds freeze on the branches. When the last note fades, the road is empty, and something lies in the dust: {item}. A whisper comes from between the trees: “Veles thanks you for listening.”

chase.text: The beggar straightens up and suddenly seems taller than the trees: “You would chase off Veles?” The ground shakes, and he melts into the mist. Your arms feel heavy as lead (curse: damage −10% for 4 fights).

coins.text: You reach for your purse, and the beggar snatches it from your hand as nimbly as a youngster and vanishes into the bushes. The purse lies abandoned a few steps further on.
coins.lossText: Some of the gold is missing from it (−{gold} gold).

song.text: The beggar plays for a long time, horribly out of tune. When he finally stops, your bag feels lighter: his accomplice must have looked inside in the meantime.
song.lossText: Some of the resources you gathered are gone ({resources}).

chase.text: The beggar springs up surprisingly briskly and runs into the forest. He leaves his hurdy-gurdy behind, and it turns out to be a plank with a string stretched across it.

haunted-shrine.title: Haunted Shrine
haunted-shrine.text: An old wayside shrine stands at a fork in the road. A candle inside burns with a pale flame, though no one lit it, and quiet weeping comes from within.

outcome.text: You walk away, and the weeping fades behind you. The candle goes out before the shrine is out of sight.

pray.text: You kneel and pray for whoever is weeping. The weeping fades, and for a moment the candle flame shines gold. Your thoughts grow clear and calm (Intellect and Wisdom +10% for 2 fights).

exorcism.text: You trace a sign and speak the words of the exorcism. The penitent soul sighs with relief and departs to where it should have gone long ago. Something is left at the foot of the shrine: {item}.

offerings.text: You sweep up the silver offerings and coins (+{gold} gold). The weeping turns into a whisper that makes your skin crawl: the soul puts a curse on you (damage −10% for 2 fights).

pray.text: You kneel to pray, but the weeping turns into a giggle. A pale figure with empty eyes slides out of the shrine. It is a Revenant!

exorcism.text: You trace a sign and speak the words of the exorcism. A Revenant flies out of the shrine with a howl and scatters like smoke before it can reach you (+{xp} XP). Where it stood, something remains: {item}.

offerings.text: You reach for the offerings, and an icy hand seizes your wrist. A Revenant guards its shrine!

pray.text: You pray in silence. The weeping turns out to be the wind in the cracks of the old boards, and the candle burns down and goes out.

exorcism.text: You speak the words of the exorcism, but nothing happens. There is no one in the shrine but spiders.

offerings.text: The weeping turns out to be the wind in the cracks of the old boards. You sweep up the silver offerings and coins that no one is guarding (+{gold} gold).

stuck-merchant.title: Merchant Stuck in the Mud
stuck-merchant.text: On the sodden road stands a cart sunk axle-deep in mud. A stout merchant in a fur hat waves his arms: “Help me, and you won't regret it!”

outcome.text: You give the cart a wide berth. The merchant goes on cursing behind your back for a long while.

help.text: You set your shoulder against the cart. At last the wheels pop out of the mud, and the merchant shakes your hand and counts out your pay (+{gold} gold): “I'll tell the Merchants' Company about you!” (+15 reputation with the Merchants' Company).

demand.text: The merchant grimaces but pays up front (+{gold} gold). You help push the cart out, and he drives off without looking back.

help.text: You set your shoulder against the cart while the merchant's helper hangs about behind your back. The cart rolls out of the mud and both of them drive off in a hurry.
help.lossText: Only then do you notice the cut strap of your purse (−{gold} gold).

demand.text: “Up front? I can see at once who I'm dealing with!” The merchant cracks his whip, the cart somehow tears free of the mud, and off he drives.

help.text: You bend over the wheel, and bandits leap out from behind the cart. The merchant in the mud was the bait!

demand.text: The merchant fumbles for words, mumbles something and glances towards the bushes. You sense the ambush before the bandits leap out of hiding.
demand.start: The bandits leap out of hiding, but the ambush no longer takes you by surprise: {enemies}.

leshy.title: The Forest Lord Twists the Path
leshy.text: The path leads you back to the same fallen oak yet again. Someone giggles behind the trees. It is the Forest Lord, master of the wilds, who loves leading travellers astray.

breaks.name: Clothes: the spell breaks
breaks.text: You turn your clothes inside out, as the old folk advise. The Forest Lord bursts out laughing until the leaves shake, and vanishes. The spell breaks, and on the trunk of the fallen oak lies his gift: {herbs}.

herbsKnown.goldText: You turn your clothes inside out, as the old folk advise. The Forest Lord bursts out laughing until the leaves shake, and vanishes. The spell breaks, and on the trunk of the fallen oak lies a handful of coins (+{gold} gold).

holds.name: Clothes: the spell holds
holds.text: You turn your clothes inside out, but the Forest Lord only giggles louder. This time the old trick fails, and you wander the forest until dusk.
holds.lossText: On the way you lose some of the resources you gathered ({resources}).

bread.label: Leave him bread and a few coins

outcome.text: You place bread and a few coins on the trunk (−{cost} gold). The giggling stops, and the branches part before you of their own accord. A shortcut leads to a hidden clearing where an old chest stands among the ferns. Inside is your reward: {item}.
You stubbornly keep going, but the path keeps turning back to the same oak. You wander until dusk, and the Forest Lord laughs from every bush.
outcome.lossText: On the way you lose some of the resources you gathered ({resources}).

outcome.text: You call into the depths of the forest for the Forest Lord to show himself and fight. The trees creak, and from between them steps a figure taller than a man, with antlers and a beard of moss.

win.text: The Forest Lord bows low and vanishes into the thicket. His gift is left on the moss: {item}.

lost-child.title: Lost Girl
lost-child.text: In the middle of the path sits a little girl in a linen shift, crying and hugging a straw doll. When she sees you, she raises her head: “I'm lost. Will you take me to my mum?”

outcome.text: The girl takes your hand. Her fingers are as cold as water from a stream. She leads you deeper and deeper into the forest until she stops before a rotten oak: “Mum lives here.” There is no hut anywhere in sight.

back.label: Let go of her hand and turn back

outcome.text: “From Willow Village, past the third stream,” the girl whispers, wiping her tears with her sleeve. The sleeve is dry, though it rained all night.

camp.label: Keep her with you for the night

food.label: Give her food and show her the way

outcome.text: You walk past the girl. Her crying stops behind you as suddenly as if someone had shut a door.

lead/look.text: Behind the oak stands a tar-burner's hut, with her mother in the doorway, hair streaming. She throws her arms around her daughter and presses a bundle with all their silver into your hands (+{gold} gold).

lead/iron.text: The girl backs away in tears and runs behind the oak, where a tar-burner's hut stands. Her mother slams the door and shouts through it that they need no madmen with knives here.

lead/back.text: You turn back to the road. The girl runs behind the oak on her own, straight to a tar-burner's hut with smoke rising from its chimney.

ask/camp.text: The girl falls asleep by the fire, hugging her doll. At dawn her father, a woodcutter from the next valley, comes for her. He thanks you at length and leaves you the most precious thing he has: {item}.

herbsKnown.goldText: The girl eats every last crumb and, to thank you, gives you a handful of small coins from her bundle (+{gold} gold). Then she runs off down the path you showed her, and a joyful shout comes from the forest: someone has found her.

ask/food.text: The girl eats every last crumb and, to thank you, gives you a basket of the herbs she was gathering before she got lost ({herbs}). Then she runs off down the path you showed her, and a joyful shout comes from the forest: someone has found her.

ask/go.text: You walk away. Behind you, you can hear the girl humming to herself as she heads towards the village.

lead/look.text: Behind the oak there is only a dug-up grave. The small hand clamps onto yours like pincers, and the girl's face turns grey and sinks in. It is a Revenant, looking for a companion in the grave!

lead/iron.text: At the sight of iron the girl screams in an inhuman voice and falls apart into a wisp of mist. Only the straw doll is left under the oak, with something sewn inside it: {item}.

lead/back.text: You let go of the cold little hand and turn back. All the way you feel an icy breath on the back of your neck, and your arms grow heavy as lead (curse: damage −10% for 2 fights).

ask/camp.text: In the night a piercing cold wakes you. The girl is standing over you with wide, empty eyes, and the fire is going out. It is a Revenant!
ask/camp.start: The Revenant falls upon you in your sleep: {enemies}.

ask/food.text: The girl takes the food but does not eat it. She smiles sadly: “No one has given me anything in a long time.” She melts away like mist, leaving you with a strange peace in your heart (focus +10% for 2 fights).

ask/go.text: You walk away briskly. The crying behind you turns into a giggle, then suddenly stops.

forest-wedding.title: Wedding in the Woods
forest-wedding.text: Music drifts from between the trees. A wedding is under way in the clearing: bonfires blaze, fiddles scrape and couples whirl in the dance. The wedding host, in an embroidered shirt, blocks your way with a horn of mead in his hand: “A guest in the house! You won't refuse the young couple?”

outcome.text: The host sits you down at the table and hands you a horn full of mead: “To the young couple's health, bottoms up!” The music plays faster and faster, and the dancers never stop for a moment, though no one looks tired.

pour.label: Secretly pour the mead under the table

gift.label: Give the young couple a gift

outcome.text: Up close it looks like an ordinary village wedding: children are pinching the wedding cake, and the bride's uncle sings out of tune. The host spots you in the bushes and waves: “Come on, join us!”

greet.label: Come out of hiding and say hello

outcome.text: You give the clearing a wide berth. The music carries through the trees for a long time after.

join/drink.text: The mead is strong and sweet. You dance with the bridesmaids until broad daylight, and when you finally set off, the wedding still hums in your veins (damage +10% for 4 fights).

join/pour.text: The host sees you pour the mead under the table and turns red with anger: “You insult the young couple!” The music stops, and you have to leave to a chorus of whistles.

join/gift.text: The bride thanks you for the gift (−{cost} gold), and the groom, a blacksmith's son, gives you something from his forge in return: {item}.

watch/greet.text: You step out of the bushes to a burst of laughter. You get a slice of wedding cake, a place by the fire and the blessing of the old matchmaker (focus +10% for 2 fights).

watch/cross.text: You cross yourself with a flourish. The wedding guests look at you as if you were mad, and someone throws a gnawed bone your way.

watch/run.text: You run into the forest. Behind you there is laughter and a jaunty ditty about a cowardly wanderer.

join/drink.text: The mead tastes of earth and smoke. You dance until the world spins and goes dark. You wake at dawn in an overgrown graveyard, an empty horn in your hand.

join/pour.text: The mead hisses on the ground like embers. The music breaks off mid-bar, and the guests turn their eyeless faces towards you. Somewhere far off a cock crows, and the clearing empties. Only some old silver tableware is left on the table (+{gold} gold).

join/gift.text: The bride takes the gift (−{cost} gold) with an icy hand: “No one has come to my wedding in a hundred years.” She takes the withered wreath from her head and hands it to you. In your fingers the wreath turns into something else: {item}. The clearing is empty.

watch.text: The longer you watch, the more you see: the fires give no warmth, and the dancers cast no shadows. The host slowly turns his head straight towards you and smiles widely, too widely.

watch/greet.text: The guests seize your hands and pull you into a round dance that never ends. When the cock crows, you are left in the empty clearing, breathless and drained.
watch/greet.lossText: The guests also took something from your bag ({resources}).

watch/cross.text: You cross yourself, and the music stops as if cut with a knife. One by one the guests bow low to you and drift away like smoke. The host vanishes last, with a grateful nod (+{xp} XP).

watch/run.text: You run, and the music follows you for a long time. No one gives chase, but you do not look back until dawn.

treasure-hunter.title: Treasure Hunter
treasure-hunter.text: A shaggy man in a patched jerkin is digging by an old barrow. When he sees you, he straightens up and waves a yellowed map: “There's robbers' treasure buried here! Help me dig and we'll split it down the middle.”

outcome.text: You dig together until dusk. At last a spade strikes the iron-bound lid of a chest. The treasure hunter puts down his spade and slowly reaches behind his belt.

wait.label: Step back and watch his hands

outcome.text: The treasure hunter pockets the coins (−{cost} gold) and hands over the map in an odd hurry. The cross on the map leads to an old pine with a hollow. Something glints inside, and there are deep, fresh scratches on the bark.

tracks.label: Examine the scratches on the bark

outcome.text: You leave the hollow alone. The map ends up in the fire, and you move on with a lighter purse.
You wish him luck and walk away. For a long time you can still hear the crunch of his spade behind you.

dig/strike.text: You strike, but he was only reaching for his flask. He flees screaming into the forest. The chest holds nothing but rotten rags, and the bad taste stays with you for a long time.

dig/open.text: Old coins glint in the chest. The treasure hunter counts them by lantern light and splits them fairly, down to the last penny (+{gold} gold).

dig/wait.text: The treasure hunter pulls a flask from behind his belt and offers you the first sip. You open the chest together: he takes the coins and leaves you what lay at the bottom: {item}.

map/reach.text: The scratches were only left by a boar rubbing against the bark. In the hollow lies a bundle wrapped in greased leather, and in it: {item}.

map/tracks.text: The scratches are a finger deep. They are claw marks, and the map turns out to be a hunting map with lairs marked on it: “{area}. The {creature} was seen there.” A hunter's purse also lies in the hollow (+{gold} gold).
map/tracks.noRumorText: The scratches were left by a boar rubbing against the bark. The map turns out to be an ordinary hunting map, and in the hollow lies a hunter's purse (+{gold} gold).

dig/strike.text: You beat him to it by the blink of an eye: a knife flashes in his hand, and his mate leaps out of the bushes with a club.
dig/strike.start: The robbers rush at you, but you strike first: {enemies}.

dig/open.text: As you lean over the chest, you feel a cold blade at the back of your neck. A second robber leaps out of the bushes. The treasure was bait!

dig/wait.text: The treasure hunter draws a knife, but sees you watching his hands. He whistles for his mate in the bushes, and they come at you together.

map/reach.text: In the hollow lies a stone wrapped in a rag. Before you can turn round, the treasure hunter is gone, and your coins with him.

map/tracks.text: The scratches are knife cuts, and a trodden path leads away from the pine. You follow it straight to a robbers' camp.
map/tracks.start: The robbers leap up from their fire: {enemies}.

dig/strike.text: Your blade passes through the treasure hunter as if through smoke. He laughs, and his face sinks into a skull. It is a Revenant, the guardian of the barrow!

win.text: Among the yellowed bones in the chest lies your prize: {item}.

dig/open.text: The chest is full of gold. As you plunge your hands into it, the treasure hunter starts to laugh, and half the coins blacken and crumble into cinders. You are left with a handful of gold (+{gold} gold) and a weight on your heart (curse: damage −10% for 4 fights).

dig/wait.text: The treasure hunter takes a clod of barrow earth from behind his belt and crumbles it between his fingers. When the dust settles, he and the chest are both gone. All that is left is the pit and a chill in your bones.

map/reach.text: In the hollow lies a yellowed skull with a coin between its teeth. When you touch it, you go cold to the marrow (curse: damage −10% for 2 fights).

map/tracks.text: The scratches form old runes. You read them and avoid the trap left by the barrow's guardian. In the hollow you find your reward: {item}.

bog-herbalist.title: Jagna in the Marsh
bog-herbalist.text: At the edge of the marsh someone is crying for help. It is Jagna, the herbalist from the Settlement: she has sunk waist-deep in black mud, and her basket of herbs bobs on the water beside her. “Help me, it’s pulling me under!”

stick.label: Hold out a stick from the bank

pull.text: You grab Jagna under the arms and pull until the mud lets go with a loud squelch. The herbalist catches her breath, fishes out her basket and presses a handful of herbs into your hands ({herbs}): “I won’t forget this” (+25 relation with Jagna).

herbsKnown.goldText: You grab Jagna under the arms and pull until the mud lets go with a loud squelch. The herbalist catches her breath and presses a few coins into your hand (+{gold} gold): “I won’t forget this” (+25 relation with Jagna).

stick.text: You hold out a long stick to Jagna and brace yourself on firm ground. Slowly the herbalist crawls out onto the bank, but her basket drifts off into the reeds. She shares what is left with you ({herbs}): “Thank you. I won’t forget this” (+25 relation with Jagna).

herbsKnown.goldText: You hold out a long stick to Jagna and brace yourself on firm ground. Slowly the herbalist crawls out onto the bank while her basket drifts off into the reeds. She presses a few coins into your hand (+{gold} gold): “Thank you. I won’t forget this” (+25 relation with Jagna).

leave.text: You walk away. Behind you the splashing and calling go on for a long while. In the evening Jagna comes back to the Settlement covered in mud: she got out on her own.

pull.text: You take her hands, and they are cold as ice. “Jagna” smiles wide: her teeth are sharp as needles and her hair is full of duckweed. A Drowned Maiden! She drags you down into the bog.
pull.start: The Drowned Maiden pulls you into the mud: {enemies}.

stick.text: You hold out the stick, and she yanks it with inhuman strength. You let go just in time. A Drowned Maiden rises from the mud, a Drowner close behind her.
stick.start: The Drowned Maiden and the Drowner crawl onto the bank, but they cannot take you by surprise: {enemies}.

leave.text: You walk away. The cries behind you turn into giggling, then into gurgling. Jagna is back at the Settlement right now, isn’t she…

star-iron.title: A Star from the Sky
star-iron.text: At night a bright star streaks across the sky and falls just beyond the hill. In the fresh crater smokes a black lump of sky-iron, and next to it hovers a lad in a leather apron: “I’m Żelisław’s apprentice. The master will pay any price for this. Will you help me carry it?”

carry.label: Help carry the iron to the forge

carry.text: You take turns carrying the lump all the way to the Settlement. Żelisław turns it in his hands like a treasure, then forges something from it for you: {item}. “I haven’t held iron like this in years” (+25 relation with Żelisław).

take.text: You push the lad aside and take the lump. A merchant on the road pays for the sky-iron without haggling (+{gold} gold). The apprentice watches you go for a long time.

leave.text: You leave the lad with his star. When you look back, he is still wrestling with the hot lump.

carry.text: You have barely lifted the lump when the lad whistles through his fingers. His friends burst out of the bushes: he is no apprentice!

take.text: You reach for the lump, and the lad whistles through his fingers. His friends burst out of the bushes, but your weapon is already in your hand.
take.start: The robbers burst out of the bushes, but they cannot take you by surprise: {enemies}.

leave.text: You walk away. Behind you there is a whistle and a rustle in the bushes: someone was waiting for someone here.

ferryman.title: The Ferryman
ferryman.text: The river has swollen after the downpour and flooded the ford. A boat rocks by the bank, and in it an old ferryman with a long pole: “I’ll take you across. But not for free.”

pay.text: The ferryman pushes off from the bank and on the way tells you what he has heard from travellers: “{area}. They say {creature} was seen there, and many a treasure with it.”
pay.noRumorText: The ferryman takes you across in silence. The water is calmer than it looked.

swim.text: You throw yourself into the icy current. It slams you against the rocks, but at last you crawl out onto the far bank. The bruises will ache for a long while (wounds: damage −10% for 2 fights).

drowner.name: Drowner in the ford
drowner.text: You wade waist-deep through the murky water when something grabs your ankle. A Drowner!

safe.name: Safe ford
safe.text: You search for shallows for a long time until you find a ford at last. You reach the far bank wet, but unharmed.

pay.text: In the middle of the river the ferryman stands up and laughs a bubbling laugh. Water drips from under his hat, and his fingers are webbed. A Nix! With one move he overturns the boat.

swim.text: You throw yourself into the icy current. It slams you against the rocks, and something laughs under the water. At last you crawl out onto the far bank, bruised to the bone (wounds: damage −10% for 2 fights).

ford.text: The ferryman watches you from under his hat for a strangely long time. You find a ford downstream and cross without trouble. When you look back, the boat is gone, and rings spread across the water.

fireside-dice.title: Dice by the Fire
fireside-dice.text: A stranger in a black hood sits by the fire, shaking a cup of dice until they rattle: “Fancy a game, traveller? Who knows, maybe luck is on your side today.”

win.name: Win
win.text: The dice roll across the stone… You win! Without a word the stranger counts out double your stake (+{gold} gold).

loss.name: Loss
loss.text: The dice roll across the stone. You lose. The stranger sweeps up the coins and smiles from under his hood (−{cost} gold).

win.name: Win
win.text: The dice spin for a long time… You win! The stranger grimaces but counts out double your stake (+{gold} gold).

loss.name: Loss
loss.text: The dice spin for a long time. You lose. The stranger sweeps your gold into his purse (−{cost} gold).

refuse.text: You shake your head. The stranger shrugs and goes back to his dice.

small.text: The dice roll strangely long and always land in the stranger’s favour. As he sweeps up the stake (−{cost} gold), the firelight shows a hoof instead of a boot. A Fiend with loaded dice!

big.text: The dice roll strangely long and always land in the stranger’s favour. As he sweeps up the stake (−{cost} gold), he throws back his hood, and horns grow from beneath it. The Fiend laughs, and his laughter drains the strength from your arms (curse: damage −10% for 4 fights).

refuse.text: You shake your head. The stranger hisses something under his breath, and as you walk away you hear the clatter of hooves behind you.

refugees.title: Burnt Out
refugees.text: At the side of the road sits a family with bundles: father, mother and two children, all smeared with soot. “Our village burned down. We have nowhere to go.”

give.label: Give them gold for a fresh start

point.label: Show them the way to the Settlement

give.text: The father shakes your hand for a long time. A few days later headman Bogumił tells everyone in the Settlement about the burnt-out family who, thanks to you, settled by the mill (+25 relation with Bogumił).

escort.text: You set off down the road together. At the fork, the way is blocked by marauders who have followed the family from the burned village.

win.text: The family reaches the Settlement safely, and headman Bogumił himself comes out to meet you (+40 relation with Bogumił).

point.text: You draw the way to the Settlement in the sand with a stick. The family thanks you and sets off.

give.text: The father tucks the gold inside his coat (−{cost} gold), and when you turn around, the family is gone. Only bundles stuffed with straw are left on the road.

escort.text: Around the first bend the “father” pulls a knife from under his rags, and the “mother” a crossbow. Robbers disguised as a burnt-out family!

point.text: You draw the way to the Settlement. The “father” thanks you, but eyes your purse strangely. As you walk away, you hear laughter behind you.

old-soldier.title: The Old Soldier
old-soldier.text: By a wayside shrine rests a grey-haired soldier with a scar across his whole face. An old, notched sword lies across his knees. “I can teach you a thing or two, for a small fee. Or spar with me, if you’re not afraid.”

outcome.text: For an hour the soldier shows you thrusts, feints and how to hold your weapon so your wrist doesn’t snap (strength: damage +15% for 6 fights).

won.name: Sparring won
won.text: After a long exchange of blows the soldier lowers his sword and laughs: “Nobody has pushed me like that in years.” He unhooks an old pouch from his belt and gives you what he has carried in it for years: {item}.

lost.name: Sparring lost
lost.text: The soldier puts you on the ground three times before you can blink. He helps you up and explains what you are doing wrong. The bump will last a long time, and the advice even longer (focus +10% for 2 fights).

outcome.text: You bow to the soldier and move on. Behind you, you hear him sharpening his sword.

companion-errand.title: [Her|His] errand
companion-errand.text: {name} suddenly stops on the road: “Wait. There’s something I have to check.”

outcome.text: “I understand,” says {name}, and follows you, but keeps looking back for a long while.

road.name: Father’s box
road.text: By an old milestone {name} suddenly stops: “Wait. My father once buried a box here for a rainy day. I have to see if it’s still here.”

together.text: You dig together under the stone. There it is! Father’s old box, and in it {item}. {name} holds his knife for a long time and finally tucks it into [her|his] belt (your bond reaches its next stage).

alone.text: {name} comes back an hour later with dirt under [her|his] nails and a smile: the box was there. [She|He] shares what was in it with you (+{gold} gold, +30 relation).

debts.name: The moneylender’s men
debts.text: {name} stops and looks at fresh tracks on the road: “Someone is following us. The moneylender’s men from town. I have to settle this at last.”

together.text: You wait together around the bend. The moneylender’s men walk straight into you.

win.text: The moneylender’s men flee and drop the promissory notes on the way. {name} tears them to shreds and laughs for the first time in ages (your bond reaches its next stage).

together.start: The moneylender’s men reach for their weapons: {enemies}.

alone.text: {name} comes back with a split lip, but calmer: “They won’t be looking for me anymore.” [She|He] presses a few coins left over from the debt into your hand (+{gold} gold, +30 relation).

farmstead.name: Land by the stream
farmstead.text: {name} points to a valley by a stream: “There. That piece of land is for sale. Will you help me look at it before someone else buys it?”

together.text: You walk the field and the woods by the stream together. The land is good. {name} drives a stick into it as a mark, and in an old fence you find something someone hid here long ago: {item} (your bond reaches its next stage).

alone.text: {name} comes back with shining eyes: the land is good, and the old farmer lowered the price. Overjoyed, [she|he] pays back an old debt to you (+{gold} gold, +30 relation).

wolves.name: The torn-eared wolf
wolves.text: {name} kneels over tracks in the mud: “It’s him. The big wolf with the torn ear, the one that killed our flock. He’s close.”

together.text: You follow the tracks together to a windfall. The wolf waits there with his pack.

win.text: The wolf falls. {name} stands over him in silence for a long time, then nods to you: “Thank you” (your bond reaches its next stage).

alone.text: {name} comes back at dusk with a wolf pelt over [her|his] shoulder, sells it at the Settlement and gives you part of the price (+{gold} gold, +30 relation).

manor.name: Messenger from the manor
manor.text: A messenger in a great lord’s colours waits on the road. {name} turns pale: “He’s here for me. The lord wants me back at the manor.”

together.text: You go to the messenger together. {name} refuses firmly but politely, and the messenger shrugs and hands over what the lord sent as a farewell: {item}. “I prefer the forest to his manor” (your bond reaches its next stage).

alone.text: {name} talks with the messenger for a long time, but comes back: “I’m not going back there.” The messenger left a purse as a farewell, and {name} shares it with you (+{gold} gold, +30 relation).

oath.name: The promise
oath.text: {name} stops by the path to an old shrine: “I promised a dying friend I would carry his sword there. But something drives away everyone who goes.”

together.text: A Revenant waits at the shrine. It is what drove everyone away.

win.text: The Revenant fades into the morning mist. {name} lays the friend’s sword beneath the shrine: “Promise kept” (your bond reaches its next stage).

alone.text: {name} comes back pale, but with a light heart: the friend’s sword now lies beneath the shrine. On the way back [she|he] pays back an old debt to you (+{gold} gold, +30 relation).

brother.name: The lost brother
brother.text: {name} picks up a scrap of red scarf: “This is my brother’s scarf! He was here not long ago.” Further on, deep into the wilds, lead the tracks of several men.

together.text: You follow the tracks together to a poachers’ camp. The brother sits tied to a tree, and the poachers reach for their weapons.

win.text: The poachers flee. {name} cuts the brother free and hugs him for a long time. The brother heads for the Settlement, and now you have two friends (your bond reaches its next stage).

alone.text: {name} comes back at dusk with news: the brother is alive and works with the charcoal burners deep in the wilds. Overjoyed, [she|he] presses the brother’s purse into your hand (+{gold} gold, +30 relation).

treasure.name: The old map
treasure.text: {name} spreads an old, frayed map across [her|his] knee: “The cross is just beyond that hill. Either it’s treasure, or someone has made a fool of me.”

together.text: You dig together under the root of an old oak. The shovel strikes a chest, and inside is {item}. {name} laughs out loud: “It was true after all!” (your bond reaches its next stage).

alone.text: {name} comes back laughing at [herself|himself]: the cross led to a hollow stump with only a few old coins at the bottom. [She|He] shares them with you (+{gold} gold, +30 relation).
